text: Freya turned five today — pancake breakfast, candles on the pancakes by her decree. Born January 2nd, 2019, our little new-year surprise.
author: Maren

text: For the record: Maren and Espen were married on December 30th, 2012, and still argue about whether the string quartet was worth it.
author: Espen

text: Otto swam his first full lap of the big pool at Saturday lessons. He was so proud he wore his goggles to dinner.
author: Espen

text: Freya is deep in a fox phase: fox books, fox drawings, a fox tail pinned to her coat.
author: Maren

text: Farmor Ingrid was born on February 29th, 1956 — a proper leap-day baby, and she will not let anyone move the celebration to March.
author: Espen

text: Otto's birthday for the family file: June 21st, born 2015. Midsummer boy — he wants a pool party every single year.
author: Maren

text: Waffle graduated from puppy class, technically. The certificate says 'participation'. Freya framed it.
author: Espen

text: Otto turned nine. Pool party, obviously: six boys, one inflatable crocodile, zero dry towels left.
author: Maren

text: Drove the four hours to Tallhaven to see Ingrid. Her garden is glorious this summer; she sent us home with rhubarb and strict instructions for it.
author: Maren

text: First band practice in the new rehearsal room. Jonas brought his old tape delay, and Petra has already booked a slot at the Old Mill autumn open stage.
author: Espen

text: Maren's birthday — September 14th, born 1986. She asked for beeswax candles and a quiet house, and got both. Barely.
author: Espen

text: Espen's birthday for the file: April 8th, 1984. He claims he doesn't want a fuss. He always wants a fuss.
author: Maren

text: A year ago on December 27th we brought Waffle home from the shelter, so December 27th is Waffle's gotcha day — a waffles-for-breakfast day forever.
author: Maren

text: Freya's kindergarten winter concert: she was a snowflake and sang the loudest by a distance. Her teacher Sara says she's the bravest in the singing circle.
author: Espen

text: New Year's Eve with a five-going-on-six-year-old: Freya made it to half past nine, which she insists counts as midnight somewhere.
author: Maren

text: Freya turned six. Fox cake by request — though she spent most of the party explaining velociraptors to Ingrid, so the fox era may be ending.
author: Maren

text: Otto has decided he is a backstroke specialist, because 'you can breathe the whole time'. Hard to argue with.
author: Espen

text: Freya finally outgrew her boots — she is in size 28 shoes now.
author: Maren

text: Otto joined the Dolphins swim club. Coach Ruth says his freestyle is raw but his kick is the strongest in the group.
author: Espen

text: Easter at Tallhaven: Ingrid hid forty-two eggs and forgot where eleven went. Waffle found nine of them.
author: Espen

text: Otto's goggles saga continues: third pair this season. Ruth suggested the strapless kind; Otto countered with a helmet.
author: Espen

text: Maren started beekeeping — two hives at the bottom of the garden. The bees, she reports, are calmer than she is.
author: Espen

text: My wife now owns more protective equipment than a hockey goalie. The bees remain unimpressed.
author: Espen

text: Otto turned ten — double digits. He asked for a swim-meet-themed cake and got Coach Ruth to sign his kickboard.
author: Espen

text: School's out, and Sara is retiring from the kindergarten after thirty years. Freya gave her a farewell drawing of the two of them as foxes.
author: Maren

text: Ingrid's hip surgery went well. She is grumbling at the physiotherapist, which the nurses say is an excellent sign.
author: Maren

text: Maren's first honey harvest came in: four jars. Freya designed the labels — a bee wearing a fox mask, naturally.
author: Espen

text: Freya started school today! Room 2 with Mr. Bakke. She informed him on day one that his dinosaur poster was 'anatomically wrong'.
author: Espen

text: Freya has officially moved on from foxes: it is dinosaurs now, full time. She corrected the museum guide about spinosaurus sails.
author: Maren

text: Old Mill open stage went brilliantly — Petra's new song earned an encore and Jonas only broke one string.
author: Espen

text: Otto's first swim meet with the Dolphins: third in backstroke! Ruth says regionals in spring are realistic if he keeps this up.
author: Maren

text: Freya's best friends this year are Liv and Noor. Important: Noor has a serious nut allergy, so nothing with nuts when she visits.
author: Espen

text: Shoe update: Freya is in size 30 now. The size 28s lasted exactly nine months.
author: Maren

text: Elm Street planting weekend: Signe organized bulbs for the whole street and Tomas lent everyone his rototiller. Six hundred tulips went in before the frost.
author: Maren

text: Freya's school winter concert: she was a triceratops in the recycling pageant. Mr. Bakke swore the costumes were waterproof. They were not.
author: Espen

text: Waffle's second gotcha day. Waffles for breakfast; the dog got scrambled eggs and a new squeaky pheasant.
author: Maren

text: Thirteen years married. We left the kids with Ingrid and had dinner at the harbor. Maren still will not concede the string-quartet argument.
author: Espen

text: Freya turned seven! Dinosaur park trip with Liv and Noor, and Ingrid baked a nut-free brachiosaurus cake so Noor could have seconds.
author: Espen

text: Otto qualified for the spring regionals in backstroke. Ruth is moving him up to the Tuesday-and-Thursday training group.
author: Maren

text: Band news: the band finally has a name — Northern Sparrows. Petra vetoed every other option, and honestly she was right.
author: Espen

text: Espen wrote me a song for Valentine's Day and swears it will never be performed in public. Good.
author: Maren

text: Celebrated Farmor Ingrid's birthday tonight, since there is no February 29th this year. Seventy years old — or seventeen and a half, by her own counting.
author: Maren

text: Big news: Ingrid sold the Tallhaven house and moved into the little apartment on Rosevik Square, ten minutes from us. No more four-hour drives.
author: Espen

text: Otto's regionals: second in 50m backstroke, four full seconds off his time. Ruth cried. Otto pretended not to notice.
author: Maren

text: Ingrid says the thing she misses most from Tallhaven is her garden. She keeps eyeing the empty planter boxes outside her building on Rosevik Square.
author: Espen

text: Second spring with the bees: Maren added a third hive. Otto helped with the smoker and only ran away twice.
author: Espen

text: Northern Sparrows are booked for the midsummer festival at the Old Mill — a full two-hour set. Jonas is already worrying about heat and his pedalboard.
author: Espen

text: Frey lost her first tooth mid-sentence while explaining ankylosaurus armor to Mr. Bakke. She was thrilled about both things.
author: Maren

text: Noor's mom taught me her nut-free brownie recipe, which makes parties much easier. Freya quality-tested six of them.
author: Maren

text: Shoe update: Freya jumped straight to size 31 shoes. Growth spurt confirmed — four centimeters since December, says the pediatrician.
author: Espen

text: Otto turned eleven. Pool party number seven, except this year the whole Dolphins group came and Ruth judged the cannonball contest.
author: Maren

text: Signe's six hundred tulips came up all along Elm Street this spring, so the street voted for a June planting weekend too. Tomas reports the rototiller has never been happier.
author: Espen

text: Ingrid has claimed the two big planter boxes outside her building. We are smuggling her old Tallhaven roses over this weekend.
author: Maren

text: Freya wants a dinosaur dig birthday next January: sandpit, buried plaster 'fossils', the works. Liv and Noor are already invited — nut-free everything, as usual.
author: Espen

text: Waffle turns out to be terrified of bees, which is awkward for a dog who lives ten meters from three hives. He now patrols only the far half of the garden.
author: Maren
